title: Keep each source's detail when merging
statement: When similar standards or sources are merged into one shared unit, keep each one's specific detail inside it, because a merged abstract description is too vague to drive lessons.
detail: The curriculum BrainLift describes an attempt to build one common graph for social studies by merging similar-looking standards from different states into unified nodes: the result was flattened abstractions that lost the specificity needed for teaching, too vague to generate good instruction (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/feedback/feedback1/Curriculum & Knowledge BrainLift.md`). The reading project's curriculum reference turned this into a rule: preserve state-specific detail inside nodes and never merge into abstract common nodes (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/skills/train-teacher/references/curriculum-architecture.md`).

evidence.quote: The result was flattened abstractions that lost the specificity needed for teaching.
**Preserve state-specific detail INSIDE nodes — never merge into abstract common nodes**
